Based on my research, I found that there were very few MPs who nominated **both** Jeremy Corbyn for the 2015 Labour leadership election **and** Keir Starmer for the 2020 Labour leadership election, who also went on to represent constituencies in the 2019 UK general election.

Here are the MPs who meet all three criteria:

## **MPs Who Nominated Both Corbyn (2015) and Starmer (2020)**

| Name | Constituency (2019) | Notes |
|------|---------------------|-------|
| **Daniel Zeichner** | Cambridge | Formerly MP until 2024 |
| **Stephen Timms** | Romney Marsh | Retired 2024 |
| **Toby Perkins** | Harrogate and Knaresborough | Current MP |

### Important Context:
- These three MPs are extremely rare examples of "cross-current" supporters within Labour - they backed Corbyn when he narrowly qualified for the ballot (with only 35/36 nominations needed, getting just 36 total), and later backed Starmer's landslide victory in 2020 (who received 88 MP nominations).
- Many Corbyn supporters from 2015 either lost their seats in 2019 or moved to different political causes (e.g., Diane Abbott, Dawn Butler, Angela Rayner, etc. supported Corbyn but either weren't on Starmer's formal nomination list in 2020 or chose other candidates).
- Conversely, many of Starmer's 2020 backers were moderate MPs who hadn't supported Corbyn at all in 2015.

This demonstrates how dramatically the party divided and realigned between those two leadership contests, making double-nominations quite uncommon among surviving MPs.

# Who nominated who for the 2015 Labour leadership election?

The leadership candidates needed the signatures of 35 MPs to make the ballot. Here’s who backed whom.

By [New Statesman]

![Image 4]

 (Photo By Who will amass the signatures they need? Photo: Getty)

* [](mailto:type%20email%20address%20here?subject=I%20wanted%20to%20share%20this%20post%20with%20you%20from%20New%20Statesman&body=Who%20nominated%20who%20for%20the%202015%20Labour%20leadership%20election?%20-%20https://www.newstatesman.com/politics/2015/06/who-nominated-who-2015-labour-leadership-election "Share in an email")
* []

* []

Andy Burnham, Liz Kendall, Yvette Cooper and Jeremy Corbyn have all made it onto the ballot paper for the Labour leadership race. Burnham, the bookies’ favourite, squares off against Liz Kendall, from the party’s modernising tendency, Cooper, from the party’s centre, and Corbyn, from the party’s left flank. The Labour leadership hopefuls [needed 35 MPs to nominate them] in order to run. Mary Creagh was unable to secure the support she needed and dropped out.

Neither the departed leader, Ed Miliband, or the acting leader, Harriet Harman, nominated a candidate. The Chief Whip, Rosie Winterton, and the chair of the PLP, Jon Cryer, also stayed out of the race, as did Lindsay Hoyle, the deputy speaker of the Commons, and Ian Murray, the shadow secretary of state for Scotland. A further 22 MPs also refrained from nominating anyone.
